binders: E : Type* is arbitrary; NormedAddCommGroup E supplies an additive commutative group with a genuine norm, and NormedSpace R E makes E a real normed vector space.
f : E -> EReal is an extended-real-valued function on all E.
V : Set E is the comparison set.
lam : R is the curvature parameter.
hf : SourceProper f says f x != bottom for every x in E, and there exist x in E and real r with f x = (r : EReal). It is global properness and has no extra topology binder.
hV : Convex R V says V contains every convex combination of its members.
hdom : V subset effectiveDomain f says f x < top for each x in V; effectiveDomain itself does not exclude bottom, but hf excludes it.
hstrong universally quantifies x in V, y in V and real a with 0 < a < 1, and bounds f(a*x+(1-a)*y) by a*f x+(1-a)*f y minus the real quantity (lam/2)*a*(1-a)*norm(x-y)^2 embedded in EReal.
p : E is a supplied point; hp : p in V ensures membership.
hmin : IsMinOn f V p means f p <= f x for every x in V. IsMinOn does not itself require p in V; hp supplies it.
q : E is an arbitrary comparison point; hq : q in V restricts comparison to V.
conclusion: (f p).toReal + (lam / 2) * norm(q - p)^2 <= (f q).toReal. This is a real inequality with exact coefficient lam/2 and squared norm.
finite_values: All values on V are neither bottom nor top by hf and hdom. Convexity puts every interpolated point in V, so hstrong also compares finite values. EReal.toReal maps either infinity to zero and a finite embedded real to itself; its infinity branches cannot occur for p, q, or these interpolated points.
arithmetic: The strong-convexity inequality uses EReal order, EReal multiplication/addition/subtraction and real-to-EReal coercions. The curvature expression is first computed entirely in R and then embedded. a and 1-a are strictly positive; lambda is nonnegative. No infinity arithmetic is needed on the stated domain.
attainment: This is conditional growth at an attained global minimum relative to V. It neither proves existence nor asserts minimization outside V. hp makes V nonempty; q is also supplied with membership.

assumptions_audit.details: hmin supplies ordinary minimum ordering, without the quadratic gap. hstrong supplies the interpolation bound. No hypothesis literally postulates the requested quadratic-growth bound. When lam = 0 the conclusion reduces to the assumed minimum ordering after finite-value conversion.
assumptions_audit.visible_restrictions: Real normed vector space, convex V, V contained in finite domain under global properness, lam >= 0, interpolation inequality on all pairs in V, and an attained minimizer. Global properness is stronger than merely requiring finiteness on V and forbids bottom even outside V. The theorem does not assume completeness, finite dimension, inner product, differentiability, continuity, closedness, compactness, or strict positivity of lam.
assumptions_audit.hidden_restrictions: No additional hidden restriction found in inspected definitions. Whether visible restrictions are supported by an external source cannot be determined in a source-blind review.
assumptions_audit.vacuity: No empty-set application is possible because hp requires p in V. Singleton V and lam=0 are allowed degeneracies, not infinity totalization. toReal infinity totalization is blocked by explicit hypotheses.
assumptions_audit.consistency: Assumptions are nonvacuously satisfiable, for example on a singleton V with a finite constant function and lam=0; this is an illustrative semantic observation, not a proof search.
